guidelines.title: Essential Dietary and Food-Drug Interactions Protocol
bullets: Grapefruit Juice & Statins/Calcium Channel Blockers: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it inhibits CYP3A4 enzymes and significantly increases serum drug concentrations.
Alcohol & NSAIDs/Acetaminophen: Avoid alcohol consumption when taking acetaminophen (liver toxicity risk) or NSAIDs (gastrointestinal mucosal bleeding risk).

Dairy/Calcium & Antibiotics: Do not take calcium-rich foods or milk simultaneously with tetracyclines or fluoroquinolones (chelates the drug and prevents intestinal absorption). Space by at least 2 hours.
High-Potassium Foods & ACE Inhibitors: Limit excessive potassium-rich foods or potassium supplements when taking ACE inhibitors or ARBs to prevent hyperkalemia.

guidelines.title: High-Risk Drug-Drug Interactions (DDI) and Safety Protocol
bullets: Anticoagulants & NSAIDs: Combining blood thinners (Warfarin, Aspirin) with NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen) exponentially increases major gastrointestinal hemorrhage risk.
Triple Whammy Danger: Simultaneous use of an ACE Inhibitor/ARB + Diuretic + NSAID severely compromises renal perfusion and can precipitate acute kidney injury.
Serotonin Syndrome Risk: Avoid combining multiple serotonergic agents (SSRIs, SNRIs, Tramadol, MAOIs) to prevent life-threatening central serotonin toxicity.
CNS Depressant Overlap: Avoid co-prescribing opioids and benzodiazepines due to additive respiratory depression and overdose risk.

guidelines.title: Clinical Guidelines for Special Patient Populations
bullets: Pregnancy & Lactation Safety: Avoid ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and NSAIDs during the 3rd trimester. Acetaminophen is generally the preferred first-line analgesic during pregnancy under medical guidance.
Geriatric Renal Monitoring: Elderly patients (>65 years) should have baseline eGFR and serum creatinine checked before starting long-term NSAIDs or renin-angiotensin blockers.
Pediatric Aspirin Avoidance: Never give aspirin to children or teenagers recovering from viral infections (chickenpox, flu) due to the risk of Reye's Syndrome.
Hepatic Impairment Dose Limits: Limit maximum daily acetaminophen dose to under 2,000 mg in patients with underlying chronic liver disease or alcohol dependency.

guidelines.title: Long-Term Management Strategies for Diabetic Neuropathy
bullets: Glycemic Control: Maintain strict blood glucose management (target HbA1c < 7.0%) to slow neuropathic progression.
Lifestyle & Physical Therapy: Regular low-impact aerobic exercise (swimming, walking) improves peripheral nerve perfusion.
Daily Foot Inspection & Care: Inspect feet daily for micro-trauma, blisters, or ulcers to prevent severe diabetic foot complications.
Multimodal Pharmacotherapy: First-line medications include SNRIs (Duloxetine) or Gabapentinoids (Pregabalin, Gabapentin).
Regular Clinical Screening: Perform annual monofilament and vibration perception testing to monitor nerve function.

guidelines.title: Lifestyle and Dietary Management of High Blood Pressure
bullets: Dietary Interventions: Follow the DASH diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy. Limit sodium under 2,000 mg/day.
Physical Activity: Engage in at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise.
Home BP Monitoring: Maintain a log of morning and evening resting blood pressure readings.
Medication Compliance: Continue prescribed antihypertensives (e.g. ACE inhibitors, Calcium Channel Blockers) consistently.
Weight Management: Achieving 5-10% weight reduction significantly lowers systolic blood pressure.

guidelines.title: Antibiotic Stewardship and Infection Recovery
bullets: Full Course Adherence: Complete the entire prescribed duration of antibiotics even if symptoms resolve early.
Hydration & Rest: Maintain optimal fluid intake and rest to support immune system clearance.
Probiotic & Gut Care: Consider probiotic support during prolonged antibiotic regimens to preserve gut microbiome balance.
Symptom Tracking: Monitor for secondary signs such as persistent fever, severe skin rashes, or allergic reactions.

guidelines.title: Multimodal Chronic Pain Management Protocol
bullets: Non-Pharmacological Therapies: Incorporate physical therapy, targeted stretching, heat/cold application, and occupational ergonomics.
Analgesic Safety: Limit NSAID use in patients with chronic kidney disease or peptic ulcer disease. Use lowest effective dose.
Renal & Hepatic Monitoring: Monitor liver function when taking acetaminophen over 3g/day.
Integrative Care: Mindfulness, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and hydrotherapy reduce central pain sensitization.

guidelines.title: Long-Term Asthma Action Plan and Management
bullets: Trigger Avoidance: Identify and minimize exposure to airborne allergens, tobacco smoke, cold dry air, and strong chemical odors.
Peak Flow Monitoring: Measure daily peak expiratory flow (PEF) to detect early airway narrowing.
Inhaler Technique: Verify proper technique for metered-dose inhalers (MDIs) with spacers to ensure optimal lung deposition.
Controller vs Rescue: Use inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) daily for controller therapy and SABA strictly for acute rescue.
